title: LastTake
tagline: Durable Strands interrupts preserve a scene's evidence until the right human can resume the wrap decision.
inspiration: Durable Strands interrupts preserve a scene's evidence until the right human can resume the wrap decision. At the end of a shoot day, the evidence needed to judge whether a scene is ready to wrap is scattered across the current script, shot list, captured takes, script supervisor's notes, camera and sound reports, continuity references and release ledger. Nobody holds all of it at once. LastTake makes missing or conflicting records visible while the script supervisor can still review them. The project uses a synthetic scene and has no observed crew trial, time saving, avoided pickup or cost result.
what_it_does: LastTake is a second set of eyes for the script supervisor and a safe decision packet for the 1st AD. A wrap checkpoint records scene.wrap-checkpoint.requested on EventBridge, then the API starts one Strands orchestrator Agent synchronously. Its eight @tool functions include four bounded evidence checks, a deterministic eligibility gate, two separate ToolContext.interrupt approval transitions and turnover publication. The checks reconcile coverage, continuity, slate and report metadata, and rights records. The gate contains no model and cannot approve wrap. S3 persists each interrupted Strands session so a later request can resume it in a different process. Approved tools publish idempotently to EventBridge. A separate rule invokes a terminal delivery-recorder Lambda that writes an immutable consumption receipt; it never starts or resumes the workflow, and its receipt proves subscriber execution rather than editorial action. A sealed, versioned turnover remains downloadable with every accepted exception still visible. Absent evidence is a finding, never a pass. Creative judgement, legal sufficiency and the actual wrap decision stay with people.
how_we_built_it: The API is one arm64 AWS Lambda behind API Gateway. It runs the Strands Agents SDK with one orchestrator Agent and eight tools. Aurora DSQL stores run state, sealed findings, decisions and handled events. S3 stores content-addressed supplied artifacts, suspended sessions, event envelopes, terminal subscriber receipts and turnover manifests. A custom EventBridge bus and rule deliver matching domain events to a least-privilege recorder Lambda with bounded retries. The React workspace is served from private S3 through CloudFront. Its service worker caches only the application shell. One tab-scoped confirmed snapshot remains read-only offline, and one unsent evidence draft can survive reload; no API response, approval or mutation is queued or replayed. Reconnect reads authoritative state and requires explicit review when its package digest changed. The public route uses a scripted planner and lexical interpreter. Bedrock mode adds two scoped interpreter Agents through the same port; Bedrock is not active in the public browser. AgentCore is not deployed. Demo-role selection is not staff authentication. GitHub Actions publishes release and acceptance receipts only after the required live journeys pass for the observed frontend and backend commits.
challenges: Strands replays a tool body from its first line on resume, so an external effect before the interrupt can fire twice. Both approval tools place publication after ToolContext.interrupt and behind an idempotency key. Event delivery is also at least once, so the terminal subscriber validates the complete envelope and conditionally creates one receipt per domain event; a conflicting receipt fails closed. Offline work needed the opposite of optimistic sync: preserve enough context to review and draft, disable every write, fetch authoritative state on reconnect, and never replay an uncertain mutation. Writing the ablation exposed two fail-open paths, both now pinned. With the interpreter unreachable, the rerunnable check moves coverage from 31 of 34 to 0 of 34 rather than inventing a pass (PYTHONPATH=src python tools/ablation.py). Human decisions bind to the exact finding digest and expire visibly when evidence changes.
accomplishments: Of 34 required beats in the fictional scene, the checkpoint reports 31 covered with evidence, 2 raising exceptions with named sources, and 1 with no release record routed to production (python -m pytest tests/test_corpus_counts.py). A recorded backend deployment test exercised a Strands pause and resume across different Lambda containers (GitHub Actions run 32606395610); source CI separately exercises two operating-system processes. The implementation includes a real EventBridge rule and terminal recorder, with deploy verification that waits for a matching consumed receipt before succeeding. A real browser journey now reloads offline from one confirmed snapshot, restores an unsent draft, observes another client's evidence change on reconnect, requires explicit revision review and sends exactly one intentional ingest. A person can then request a distinct human wrap approval and publish a sealed turnover whose manifest and portable receipt carry the run, policy version, evidence digest and open items.
what_we_learned: Several defects were found only by reading deployed output: a browser test on the live URL, a curl of the API, or a grep of the served bundle. Absent evidence has to be a finding at every layer, including the interface, or a reassuring screen becomes the failure.
what_is_next: A practising script supervisor walkthrough that no automated journey replaces; staff identity and authorization rather than the explicitly unauthenticated demo-role selector; one real production input format with a safe preview; and Bedrock on the public path only if its semantic value over the lexical reader is measured against the frozen cases in docs/model-evidence-protocol.json. A production offline design would need authenticated multi-device conflict resolution; this release intentionally provides bounded review and draft continuity without mutation replay.
limits_stated_plainly: The corpus is synthetic: THE LAST FERRY is a fictional production and the packet says so on its face.
No footage or audio is analysed. Sound checks reconcile supplied metadata only.
Nothing is legally cleared by this system; a verified rights row means the expected record was found and its fields matched policy.
No practising script supervisor has run it. Automated journeys are not user validation.
Human active time, interruptions and corrections are unmeasured; timing a model and calling it human time saved would be a fabricated benchmark.
Offline mode is one tab-scoped confirmed snapshot and one unsent draft. It is read-only until authoritative reconnect and never queues or replays a mutation.
Demo roles are not authenticated staff identities. AgentCore is not deployed.
A consumed EventBridge receipt proves the terminal recorder ran. It does not prove editorial delivery or cause the Strands workflow to run.
